table_9_3.note: not in EDM 2026 Table 9-3; a class is never inferred (R16 / R17); drawn grey, no need-box

city.match_rule: genus == ACER and first species word == PLATANOIDES; hybrid marker 'X' ignored; any cultivar

height_m.note: City height_m values are class midpoints (4.6, 7.6, 10.7 …), not measurements

form.note: assigned by the author from horticultural common knowledge; replaced when a cited reference is entered

literature.source: City of Vancouver Street Tree Guidelines 2011, pp.12–14
literature.definition_as_printed: Trees over 50 ' in height and 25 ' in width. Suitable for boulevards with no overhead obstructions and > 10 ' of width.
literature.note: a class threshold, not a per-species value: the drawn crown still uses the nominal ratio; the only width the City prints is 'over 25 ft' for Large

crown_width.note: crown spread is not published by the City; ratio by form until a cited value replaces it; Guidelines 2011 give only a class threshold (see literature), so the ratio stays nominal

reference.collection: Root System Drawings (Wageningen University & Research, Image Collections)
reference.publication: Kutschera, L.; Lichtenegger, E., Wurzelatlas mitteleuropäischer Waldbäume und Sträucher. Graz, Stuttgart: Leopold Stocker Verlag, 2002 (2. Aufl. 2013), 604 p.
reference.reading_rule: per plate the atlas records the excavated plant's root depth (D root) and root-system diameter; the mean ratio depth / diameter over plates of plants at least 5 m tall (all plates when none is) gives the drawn habit: >= 0.40 tap, 0.15–0.40 heart, < 0.15 flat
reference.rights: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 for the Wurzelatlas information and illustrations (source quoted in full, non-commercial, publisher informed); the scans of the original drawings need the heirs' permission (wurzelforschung.at)

root_form.note: root habit read from the atlas plates (Kutschera & Lichtenegger 2002) for the drawing only; the plates are excavated Central-European specimens: not a measured extent on the site; roots are still drawn only in the soil the rule credits

guidelines_2011.cite: City of Vancouver Street Tree Guidelines 2011, Preferred Street Tree Species List pp.12–14 (Columnar, Large, Small)

class_definitions.Large: Trees over 50 ' in height and 25 ' in width. Suitable for boulevards with no overhead obstructions and > 10 ' of width.
class_definitions.Small: Trees maturing twenty-five (25) feet. Suitable for locating at or below overhead electrical conductors
class_definitions.Columnar: Trees exhibiting a distinct upright branch arrangement. Suitable for locating in confined situations or on tree lawns offset from overhead electrical conductors.

guidelines_2011.note: a 2011 City guideline list (species-level cultivars as printed); EDM 2026 Table 9-3 is the rule the tool applies

drawn_height_m.basis: p90 of City height_m over 12734 trees of this species
drawn_height_m.note: nine in ten City trees of this species are this tall or shorter; class midpoints, not a mature size

model.note: trunk cylinder + faceted crown hull, no branching; normalized to height 1.0 and scaled by the tree's height on the page
